text:
maria: Hey folks — noticed a recurring pattern in the sampleapp onboarding run: when a user does the initial parallel imports we see the client SDK ramp up quickly, server responds with intermittent 429s, then the client backs off in a way that causes the app to reissue the same page requests and we get pricing spikes + duplicated work. Anyone seen this?
ravi: yep saw that in last night's e2e. Pretty much a 'ping-pong' between client-side window growth and server-side rate enforcement.
tj: can you paste a small request/response trace? curious whether the SDK is honoring Retry-After vs doing its own exponential backoff.
maria: trace excerpt: 
```
POST /v1/embeds/batch 200ms
X-Rate-Limit-Reset: 12
<- 429 Retry-After: 1\n<- body: {"code":"rate_limit","hint":"burst"}
```
maria: client then waits 1s, retries both pages, server queues them and returns 429 again. Cycle repeats.
sarah: hmm. SDK behavior differs across languages — JS uses jittered backoff with a slow-start window, Go uses fixed increments. That mismatch could explain why some onboarding runs blow up more on node-based sampleapps.
ravi: we also saw stale client-side cache of 'remaining' counters — two parallel workers read 10 tokens remaining and both proceed, so concurrent oversubscription.
tj: two angles: 1) change SDK defaults to a small initial window (slow-start) + max-inflight limiter per logical session; 2) server can return a queue-position or a soft-shed header to help clients pace.
sarah: agree. Also the JS SDK's jitter seed bug (seed=0 sometimes) makes jitter reduce to near-zero in some environments — that's an SDK parity bug. We should surface an alert if jitter entropy is insufficient.
ci-bot: New issue created: INF-4221 "slow-start defaults + queue-position header" and assigned to @ravi and @sarah :white_check_mark:
ravi: I'll take adding a per-session inflight cap option to the SDKs (config name: maxInFlightPerSession). I'll prototype in go-sdk and js-sdk.
sarah: I'll own server-side header (X-Queue-Position) and a doc block describing recommended client pacing algorithm. Also will add a small sampleapp demonstrating a 'graceful slow-start' flow.
tj: For immediate mitigation, can we tweak sampleapp to use a lightweight local leaky-bucket before hitting the SDK? Something like: acquire token from local bucket; if unavailable, enqueue UI job for 50-200ms and try again. Keeps bursts from hammering server.
maria: put a tiny code snippet in UX repo? small example for mobile/web onboarding flows.
sarah: also propose SDK telemetry emit when retries > 3 in short window so we can alert on onboarding churn.
ravi: noted. Will also add a test in the e2e harness that simulates parallel imports to validate slow-start prevents duplication.
tj: one more thought — server could include a deterministic backoff factor per session so clients don't fight. Maybe X-Client-Backoff: 1.5 meaning multiply base backoff by that factor.
sarah: nice. add to INF-4221 as optional header.
maria: thanks y'all. Will coordinate sampleapp updates and link PRs here. :thumbsup:
